skill.name: database-guardrails
skill.description: Plans database-backed changes with an ask-first safety gate, minimal schema growth, programmatic versioned migrations, and evidence-based indexes. Use for database modeling, schema changes, migrations, data repair, or database performance work; do not access or change a database by default.
skill.summary: Guides minimal database designs and reviewed migrations while requiring explicit approval before live database access.
skill.author: shreyam1008

content.user_title: Plan Database Changes With Explicit Approval
content.value_statement: Database changes can damage data when scope, recovery, and permissions are unclear. This skill guides minimal schema designs and reviewed migration plans before authorized database access.
actual_capabilities: Requires explicit authorization for the database target, operation, and scope before live access.
Prompts for ownership, retention, compatibility, concurrency, and recovery requirements before schema design.
Guides minimal tables, columns, relationships, and constraints for one bounded workflow.
Requires a named query, constraint, or measured problem to justify each index.
Directs changes through reviewed, versioned migrations rather than startup mutations or improvised SQL.
Structures verification and reporting around migration artifacts, checks, approval, actions taken, and rollback paths.
limitations: Provides agent instructions, not technical enforcement of database permissions.
Includes no executable migration runner or automated database test suite.
Requires project context and user answers to resolve ownership, schema requirements, and authorized scope.
Does not prescribe database-specific SQL syntax or guarantee migration safety and performance.

use_cases.title: Design a Minimal Persistence Model
use_cases.description: Clarify one application workflow and propose only necessary schema changes without accessing a live database.

use_cases.title: Review a Production Migration Plan
use_cases.description: Check authorization, recovery, locking, backfills, and disposable upgrade tests before approving migration execution.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Proposed Indexes
use_cases.description: Review query justification, selectivity, existing coverage, storage, and write costs before retaining an index.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Database Request
prompt_templates.prompt: I need persistence for [workflow]. Ask about requirements and ownership before proposing a schema. Do not connect to or query any database.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish requirements and approval boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Propose a Minimal Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository schema for [workflow]. Propose the smallest necessary change and its integrity constraints. List open questions and avoid live database access.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: design within an existing persistence model.

prompt_templates.title: Justify an Index Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [query description] and the repository indexes. Explain candidate indexes, selectivity assumptions, duplicate coverage, and write costs. Request authorization before obtaining live query plans.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess performance changes using documented evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Migration Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a versioned migration plan for [change] using repository conventions. Cover backfills, locking, idempotency, disposable tests, recovery, and approval needed. Do not execute database actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare an upgrade artifact and execution review.

output_examples.input: Add persistence for customer delivery preferences without accessing a database.
output: Known facts: Live database access is not authorized; existing schema ownership remains unknown.
Minimal proposal: Reuse the customer model if its ownership and compatibility support the required preference.
Open questions: Which values are valid, can preferences be absent, and what retention requirements apply?
Migration artifact: Pending repository review and clarified requirements.
Approval needed: Specify the target, operation, and scope before any live access.

output_examples.input: Review a proposal to index every column in the orders table.
output: Known facts: No named queries or measured performance problems were supplied.
Minimal proposal: Do not add blanket indexes; identify actual filters, joins, ordering, and uniqueness requirements.
Open questions: What are the expected selectivity, existing index coverage, write volume, and storage costs?
Approval needed: Explicit permission is required before collecting live query plans.

best_practices: Specify the exact database target, operation, and permitted side effects before authorizing access.
Start with repository artifacts and one bounded workflow before expanding the schema.
Review versioned migrations, recovery steps, and disposable fresh-install and upgrade tests before execution.
anti_patterns: Treating a general development request as permission to inspect or mutate a live database.
Adding speculative tables, generic data models, or indexes without concrete requirements.
Running unreviewed SQL, changing applied migrations, or silently modifying schema during application startup.

faq.question: Does the skill access a database automatically?
faq.answer: Its instructions prohibit live access unless the user explicitly authorizes the exact target, operation, and scope.

faq.question: Does it enforce permissions technically?
faq.answer: No. It provides behavioral instructions for the agent. Database credentials and access controls still require independent configuration.

faq.question: What can happen before database approval?
faq.answer: The agent can review repository code, schema files, migration history, documentation, and synthetic or disposable fixtures.

faq.question: What if the project has no migration system?
faq.answer: It directs the agent to create a scoped migration artifact with dry-run, recovery, and execution instructions before any authorized run.

faq.question: How does it decide whether an index is needed?
faq.answer: Each index needs a named query, constraint, access path, or measured problem, with selectivity and operational costs considered.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a safe production migration?
faq.answer: No. Safety depends on project-specific review, explicit authorization, recovery readiness, and fresh-install and upgrade testing in disposable environments.
